title: SkyLink exports protocol mechanisms to other chains, not just bridged token balances
content:
A.4.2 defines SkyLink as "a multichain system that enables native crosschain transfer of Sky Ecosystem-related tokens to other blockchains, including Ethereum L2s and major L1s." A.4.2.1 then states what travels with the tokens: "SkyLink deployments support features including the Savings Rate Mechanism (including sUSDS), the Token Rewards Mechanism and the SKY Staking Mechanism."

The distinction matters because the default multichain stablecoin design ships only a claim — a wrapped token on the destination chain that earns nothing and does nothing until bridged home. Under that design, every yield-bearing or reward-bearing behaviour stays on mainnet, and remote users are second-class holders who must pay bridge costs to participate in the economics.

SkyLink instead replicates the mechanisms themselves, so a user on Solana or Avalanche can hold sUSDS and accrue the Savings Rate, or stake SKY, without returning to Ethereum. USDS becomes genuinely multi-homed rather than mainnet-with-satellites.

The cost is that each mechanism now has N deployments to maintain, audit and keep parameter-synchronized, and each destination chain inherits a copy of the attack surface. That is precisely why the rest of A.4.2.2 is almost entirely freeze authority, rate limits and validator quorums: replicating mechanisms multiplies what can go wrong, so the containment machinery has to be standardized.
description: Deployments carry the Savings Rate (including sUSDS), Token Rewards and SKY Staking natively, so a remote chain hosts the product rather than a wrapped IOU of it.
